handoff_instructions.purpose: Handoffs document the current state and scope of the project so a new LLM session can pick up exactly where the last one left off. They are the primary continuity mechanism for this project.
what_to_include: A summary of what was done, discussed, decided, or built in this session
What worked and what did not work
Current pipeline state — what scripts exist, what their status is, what the next steps are
A condensed recap of prior sessions so the new LLM has full project context without reading every previous handoff
Open questions or blockers that carry into the next session
what_not_to_include: Exhaustive code listings — reference file paths instead
Decisions that were reversed or abandoned mid-session — only document final state
Decisions that were reversed or abandoned mid-session — only document final state
Speculation about distant future work — stay close to what is actually next
format_rules: This handoff_instructions block must appear at the top of every future handoff
When a user says 'create a handoff for this session,' use this block as the template and fill in the session-specific fields
Prior session summaries should be condensed — one paragraph per session, not a full retelling
Be brief but complete. A new LLM should be able to start working immediately after reading this file

derivation_rules.sewer_services_from_lot_count: 7/9 jobs within 10% — HIGH confidence. Forest Grove PH2 (phase 2 job) and 6th Ave are exceptions.
derivation_rules.water_services_from_lot_count: 7/8 jobs within 10% — HIGH confidence. Same exceptions.
derivation_rules.drywells_from_lot_count: 0/10 jobs — BROKEN RULE. Drywells do not track lot_count (actual ratio 0.09–0.50 per job). They track road drainage, not lots.
derivation_rules.sewer_manholes_from_sewer_LF: 9/10 jobs within 25% of qty = sewer_main_LF / 250 — MEDIUM confidence.

what_was_done_this_session.eda_notebook_built: Built phase1/knowledge_pack/generate_eda_notebook.py — a generator script that produces eda.ipynb. The notebook has 37 cells, all passing (0 errors). eda_notebook_sections.1_job_overview: Bar charts for total/lots/road_LF. Scatter: total vs lots (r~0.85) and total vs road_LF (r~0.78). Total is better correlated with lot_count than road_LF.
eda_notebook_sections.2_item_presence_matrix: Heatmap of which items appear in which jobs. Items in ALL 11 jobs: UTILITY TRENCHING, CONSTRUCTION ENTRANCE, INLET PROTECTION.
eda_notebook_sections.3_unit_price_distributions: Box plots by category + CV% table. Tightest distributions: ROLLED CURB (CV 13.7%), STRIP ROW TO STOCKPILE (CV 13.8%), 8" WATER MAIN PVC (CV 17.9%). Most variable: SIGNS & STRIPING, SUBGRADE ROAD.
eda_notebook_sections.4_item_scale_pearson_r: Heatmap of every measurable item qty vs lot_count/road_LF/ROW_SF. Strongest lot_count correlates: 4" sewer services, 1" water services, single drywells, fire hydrants. Strongest road_LF correlates: utility trenching, sewer main, water main, curb/gutter.
eda_notebook_sections.5_cross_item_correlations: Clustered correlation matrix for EA+LF items N>=4. 85 pairs with |r|>=0.70. Top finding: 1" water services ↔ 4" sewer services r=1.000 (perfect). Also: 1" water services ↔ irrigation sleeves r=0.999. These item clusters are the 'travel together' patterns Nolan flagged.
eda_notebook_sections.6_deep_dives: Sewer vs water scatter (confirms r=1.0). Drywells 4-panel (vs lot_count, road_LF, scuppers, sewer_svc) — road_LF is the best correlate but still noisy. LF items vs road_LF: utility trenching r~0.97, sewer main r~0.95, water main r~0.92, curb r~0.85. Fire hydrants vs road_LF r~0.83.
eda_notebook_sections.7_price_trends: Unit price vs date for N>=8 items. CONSTRUCTION ENTRANCE, UTILITY TRENCHING, INLET PROTECTION are very stable 2023–2026 (near-zero slope). No strong inflation signal in measurable items — but dataset is only 3 years.
eda_notebook_sections.8_job_type_signatures: $/lot: min=$11,726, P25=$31,072, median=$35,873, P75=$47,914, max=$109,765. $/road_LF: see patterns_review.md. Slight negative correlation between lot_count and $/lot — possible economies of scale but noisy with only 10 jobs.
eda_notebook_sections.9_cost_contribution: Added mid-session after user asked about TOTAL AREA ROW. Category-level stacked bar (ROADS_PAVING 15–59%, EARTHWORK 5–20%, WATER 8–12%, CONCRETE_FLATWORK 5–12%). True Pareto (no N filter) showing earthwork LS items that were invisible in the N>=3 table. Bellwether analysis: ext_price Pearson r vs job total.

ls_item_analysis_key_insight.trigger: User noticed TOTAL AREA ROW was missing from the top-30 cost contribution table. This item lives in qty sheets, not proposals. Led to a deep architectural discussion about LS item inference.
ls_item_analysis_key_insight.finding: Many earthwork items are '1 LS $X' in proposals with no exposed quantity. The underlying quantity (ROW_SF × stripping_depth → CY) lives in the qty sheets. Back-calculating $/CY reveals a very tight rate across 5 jobs.
ls_item_analysis_key_insight.conclusion: Onsite stockpile rate is $2.20–$3.83/CY. Haul-off adds ~3–4x (Solara: $9.24/CY). An LLM with ROW_SF=134,558 and depth=18" computes 7,475 CY × $2.50–3.00 = $18.6k–$22.4k vs actual $22,000. Bullseye.
ls_item_analysis_key_insight.haul_off_flag: Haul-off vs onsite stockpile is readable from proposal text. Flag it and multiply rate by 3–4x.

partially_inferable: Exc to Embank: depends on cut/fill volumes from grading plan. Without grading plan, use analog earthwork % (5–15% of total). Wide variance.
Subgrade Road: risk/contingency item. Range $3k–$21k with NO correlation to any scale metric. Use analog retrieval.
not_inferable: Clear Trees / Demo Buildings: entirely site-specific
ls_item_inference_framework.architectural_implication: Analog retrieval handles non-inferable LS items better than $/unit formulas. Find the 2–3 closest historical jobs by lot_count + road_LF, use their LS earthwork costs adjusted for scale. Neither analog retrieval alone nor $/unit alone is sufficient — use both.

open_questions: Qty sheet structure: are all 12 qty sheets in a consistent enough Excel layout that one parser can handle them, or are they each unique? This determines whether enhance-parse_qty_sheet.py is feasible vs. job-specific manual extraction.

Forest Grove PH2 has zero earthwork in its proposal ($0 earthwork category). Is this because it's a Phase 2 job where the ROW was already stripped in Phase 1, or is the earthwork scoped differently? Affects how to interpret its total and $/lot.
6th Ave and Boyds Landing have no confirmed ROW_SF or stripping depth. Do their qty sheets have TOTAL AREA ROW? Needed to include them in Type 2 rate calculations.

Subgrade Road LS: ranges $3k–$21k with no correlation to scale metrics. Is this genuinely a risk/contingency allowance, or does Terra Underground have an internal calculation method for it? If the latter, it might be inferable with more context.

The drywells rule (0/10 on lot_count) needs a replacement rule. EDA shows moderate road_LF correlation. Is there a design standard for drywell spacing (e.g., 1 per X LF of road) that Nolan can confirm?

Knowledge pack market metadata: should the knowledge pack explicitly list which jobs are confirmed Hayden/Kootenai County vs. uncertain location? 6th Ave and Boyds Landing location unknown — does Nolan know where these are?

important_architectural_decisions_made_t.two_rate_class_model: The knowledge pack must contain two distinct rate classes: (1) proposal-backed $/unit for measurable items, and (2) qty-sheet-backed $/base_unit for LS items. Without both, LS earthwork items are either wrong or missing from estimates.
important_architectural_decisions_made_t.analog_retrieval_is_primary_for_unknowns: Non-inferable LS items (clear trees, rock allowances, site-specific work) should be handled via analog retrieval, not formula. The formula approach only works for items with a measurable quantity driver.
important_architectural_decisions_made_t.market_specificity: The knowledge pack must be labeled as North Idaho / 2023–2026 baseline. Rates should never be presented as universal. Fuel-sensitive items flagged as most volatile.
important_architectural_decisions_made_t.eda_notebook_is_exploratory_not_final: With 11 jobs, all statistical findings are directional. Patterns will tighten as job count grows toward ~50. The notebook should be re-run as new jobs are added to the case library.
